steps.title: Open the network settings
steps.text: Open Settings, Network & internet, then Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and open the properties of that connection.

steps.title: Make DNS manual
steps.text: Next to DNS server assignment choose Edit, pick Manual and turn IPv4 on.

steps.title: Enter the addresses
steps.text: Put the first one in Preferred DNS and the second in Alternate DNS.

steps.title: Require encryption
steps.text: For both servers set DNS encryption to Encrypted only (DNS over HTTPS). If it asks for a manual template, give it this address.

steps.title: Save
steps.text: Press Save. Encrypted only stops Windows from falling back to unencrypted DNS for the IPv4 servers you entered. If your network also hands out IPv6 DNS, untick Internet Protocol Version 6 in the properties of the connection, or those servers keep working unencrypted and outside this Endpoint.

steps.title: Check the setup
steps.text: A few seconds after saving, run this check to see that the device uses this Endpoint.

steps.title: Allow this network
steps.text: Plain DNS only works for a network whose address you have claimed. Turn Plain DNS on for the Endpoint, then claim and prove this network's address on the Addresses page.

steps.title: Open the network adapters
steps.text: Open Control Panel, Network and Sharing Center, then Change adapter settings.

steps.title: IPv4 properties
steps.text: Right-click your connection, choose Properties and open Internet Protocol Version 4.

steps.title: Enter the addresses
steps.text: Choose Use the following DNS server addresses. Put the first in Preferred and the second in Alternate.

steps.title: Encrypt in your browser
steps.text: Windows 10 has no system-wide encrypted DNS. For encryption, set up your browser with its own guide as well.

steps.title: Check the setup
steps.text: A few seconds after saving, run this check to see that the device uses this Endpoint.
